question.text: Under the new tax regime for FY 2025-26, Arjun has a total income of Rs.12,40,000 (after standard deduction). His computed income tax before rebate is Rs.68,000. What is his final income tax liability after applying Section 87A rebate and marginal relief?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the FY 2025-26 new regime, Section 87A rebate is available only if total income does not exceed Rs.12,00,000. Arjun's income of Rs.12,40,000 is above this threshold, so the 87A rebate is not available. Marginal relief, however, applies for income up to Rs.12,71,250: tax payable cannot exceed the income above Rs.12,00,000. Here that cap is Rs.12,40,000 - Rs.12,00,000 = Rs.40,000. Comparing the computed tax of Rs.68,000 with the marginal-relief cap of Rs.40,000, the final tax is limited to Rs.40,000. The Trap: Rs.68,000 ignores marginal relief. Rs.0 wrongly applies the 87A rebate even though income exceeds Rs.12,00,000. Rs.8,000 wrongly computes Rs.68,000 minus a Rs.60,000 rebate. Note: Once total income exceeds Rs.12,00,000, the 87A rebate is gone; marginal relief then caps the tax at the excess of income over Rs.12,00,000 within the relief band.
